ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The bottom wire of the attached circuit is grounded. There are two nodes a and b above, R5 is connected between node a and node b, marked as 1 Ω, and the arrow of branch current I5 points from a to b. There are two branches from node a to ground: one is R2=1 Ω directly grounded, and the other is R1=1 Ω in series with a 12 V voltage source, with the upper terminal of the voltage source positive, the lower terminal negative, and connected to the bottom ground wire. There are three branches from node b to ground: an R3 branch, a 16 A current source branch with the arrow upward pointing to node b, and an R4=1 Ω branch. Reasoning: Let the bottom wire be the reference ground. Because the problem states I5=0, and R5=1 Ω, there is no voltage drop across R5, therefore Va=Vb; at the same time, the R5 branch can be removed when writing KCL. Write KCL for node a: the current through R2 is Va/1, and the current through the branch of R1 in series with the 12 V source is (Va-12)/1. Node a has no external current source injection, so Va/1+(Va-12)/1=0, obtaining 2Va-12=0, therefore Va=6 V. From Va=Vb, Vb=6 V is obtained. Write KCL for node b: the 16 A current source injects upward into node b, and this 16 A must flow to ground through R4 and R3. The current through R4 is Vb/1=6 A, and the current through R3 is Vb/R3=6/R3. Therefore 16=6+6/R3, obtaining 10=6/R3, so R3=6/10=0.6 Ω.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, find the value of \(R_3\) when the current \(I_5\) in the branch containing \(R_5\) is zero.

method.method_draft: Set the bottom conductor as ground. Since I5 = 0 through R5, impose Va = Vb and remove the R5 branch from the KCL equations. Write KCL at node a: current through R2 plus current through the R1–12 V source branch must sum to zero, so Va/1 + (Va - 12)/1 = 0, giving Va = 6 V. Therefore Vb = 6 V. Write KCL at node b: the 16 A source entering node b must leave through R4 and R3, so 16 = Vb/1 + Vb/R3. Substitute Vb = 6 to get 16 = 6 + 6/R3, hence R3 = 0.6 Ω.

推理：令底部导线为参考地。因为题设 I5=0，且 R5=1 Ω，所以 R5 上无电压降，因此 Va=Vb；同时在列 KCL 时可去掉 R5 支路。对节点 a 写 KCL：通过 R2 的电流为 Va/1，通过 R1 与 12 V 电源串联支路的电流为 (Va-12)/1。节点 a 无外部电流源注入，所以 Va/1+(Va-12)/1=0，得到 2Va-12=0，因此 Va=6 V。由 Va=Vb，得 Vb=6 V。对节点 b 写 KCL：16 A 电流源向上注入节点 b，这 16 A 需经 R4 和 R3 流向地。通过 R4 的电流为 Vb/1=6 A，通过 R3 的电流为 Vb/R3=6/R3。因此 16=6+6/R3，得到 10=6/R3，所以 R3=6/10=0.6 Ω。

method.method_draft: Treat R5 as an open circuit because I5 = 0. First find the open-circuit voltage at terminal a of the left subnetwork. With R1 = R2 = 1 Ω and the top of the voltage source fixed at +12 V, terminal a is the midpoint between a 1 Ω path to 12 V and a 1 Ω path to ground, so Va = 12 × 1/(1 + 1) = 6 V. For no current in R5, terminal b must also be 6 V. Now analyze the right subnetwork alone: the 16 A current source feeds the parallel conductances of R4 = 1 Ω and R3, so Vb = 16 /(1/1 + 1/R3). Set this equal to 6 V and solve: 6 = 16 /(1 + 1/R3), giving R3 = 0.6 Ω.
